difficulty.notes: The anchor is the slide-captcha success callback in loginbypassword20231031.js (the function containing the captured 1.json code at line 369), which assembles jQuery.ajax({url:'/loginwithpwdStrong.api', data:{uid, pwd: encryptedString(key_to_encode, password), ...}}). There is NO app-level rsa() wrapper (contrast case5): the login code calls the generic RSA primitive encryptedString directly with a global key, so encryptedString is a 0.5 Core utility and the 0.7 tier is empty. RSA.min.js holds the BigInt RSA primitives. A near-identical first login attempt (no-captcha, ~line 233) and the initSlideMathCode setup are sibling/containing functions; initSlideMathCode contains the anchor and so scores 1.0 by containment.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The slide-captcha success callback in loginbypassword20231031.js that assembles the login request and writes pwd: encryptedString(key_to_encode, password); it is the complete function containing the captured 1.json code (line 369). encryptedString/RSAKeyPair are generic RSA primitives (0.5); no app-level password encryptor exists so the 0.7 tier is empty.

behavior_category.subtype: RSA (BigInt impl) of password called directly with a global key
behavior_category.recompute_check: legacy RSA padding behavior not asserted; static localization only

near_categories.why_not: Only the scalar password is encrypted, not the whole request body.
The token is RSA of user input, not a device/browser digest.

evidence: The anchor is an inline captcha-success callback reached indirectly (first login attempt -> error count -> initSlideMathCode -> captcha success); the RSA primitives live in a separate single-line minified RSA.min.js.

The assembly callback (anchor) vs encryptedString/RSAKeyPair (RSA primitives, 0.5) vs decryptedString/biMultiply, plus a near-identical no-captcha first login attempt (~line 233), are easy to confuse.

provenance.label_points_to: the slide-captcha success callback (~line 369) that assembles the login request with pwd: encryptedString(...) — this is the anchor; encryptedString is the 0.5 RSA primitive it calls
